steps.title: Obtain approval and select mice
steps.instruction: Secure institutional animal‑procedure approval. Use C57BL/6J mice of both sexes, 8–12 weeks old (C57BL/6N may also be used). Keep injection time consistent (e.g., 9 a.m.) and plan tissue collection 4 h after the final treatment.

steps.title: Prepare KXA anesthetic solution
steps.instruction: Combine 2 mL ketamine (100 mg/kg), 1 mL xylazine (10 mg/kg) and 0.6 mL acepromazine (3 mg/kg) with 3 mL 0.9 % (w/v) NaCl saline. Vortex 30 s. The solution should appear yellow, be free of precipitate, and can be stored ≤2 weeks at 4 °C.

steps.title: Weigh mice and calculate dose
steps.instruction: Weigh each mouse on a fine scale. Calculate injection volume as 33 µL per 10 g body weight (e.g., a 30 g mouse receives 99 µL of the KXA solution). Adjust for each animal’s exact weight.

steps.title: Load syringe and inject intraperitoneally
steps.instruction: Draw the calculated KXA volume into a 1 mL syringe fitted with a 26 G needle. Grasp the mouse by the neck, turn it onto its back, and insert the needle at a 45° angle into the lower right quadrant of the peritoneal cavity (avoid the linea alba). Keep the head tilted down, inject, then release the mouse back into its home cage. Ensure no leakage or subcutaneous accumulation.

steps.title: Monitor anesthesia and maintain temperature
steps.instruction: After injection, expect a 1–2 min hyper‑excitation phase followed by loss of consciousness. Induction takes 5–10 min; the surgical plane lasts ≈40 min. Apply eye ointment. Confirm anesthesia by: (i) absent toe‑pinch reflex (~10 min post‑induction), (ii) reduced respiratory rate, (iii) no response to noxious stimuli, (iv) flaccid paralysis, (v) no whisker movement. Keep the mouse at 37 °C with a heating pad or red lamp, checking temperature regularly with a thermometer.

steps.title: Allow recovery and return to cage
steps.instruction: When the mouse regains righting reflex and normal activity, return it to the animal facility with food and water ad libitum. If multiple mice share a cage, verify that all are awake before leaving to prevent aggression.

steps.title: Repeat KXA injections as required
steps.instruction: Perform steps 2–6 every 2–3 days, at least twice and up to six times, to achieve the desired reduction in PNN‑coated cells (≈80 % loss after 3×–6× KXA). Maintain the same injection time (e.g., 9 a.m.) for each session.

steps.title: Assemble 60‑Hz light stimulation box
steps.instruction: Use a black plastic box (60 × 40 × 32 cm, ≈62 L). Attach LED strip horizontally along the inner walls in six layers, spaced 4 cm apart, from top to bottom for even illumination. Build the circuit on a breadboard: insert a transistor (ground pin on the right), connect breadboard ground to transistor ground, place a 200 Ω resistor between breadboard ground and the transistor’s left pin, connect Arduino GND to breadboard ground, connect Arduino digital pin 5 to the transistor’s left pin (through the resistor), wire LED red (+) to Arduino Vin, wire LED black (‑) to the transistor’s middle pin, solder fine‑strand leads if needed and insulate joints with electrical tape, then connect a 12 V power supply to the Arduino jack.

steps.title: Install Arduino IDE and connect board
steps.instruction: Download and install the Arduino IDE (https://www.arduino.cc/en/main/software). Connect an Arduino/Genuino UNO to the computer via a USB Type A/B cable.

steps.title: Program Arduino for 60‑Hz flicker
Program Arduino for constant light control
Verify output frequency
steps.instruction: Connect an oscilloscope to Arduino digital pin 5 and confirm a 60 Hz square‑wave (≈8.3 ms high, 8.3 ms low).

steps.title: Position mouse cage in stimulation box
steps.instruction: Place the mouse cage at the marked central position inside the LED box (use tape to mark). Up to four animals may be stimulated simultaneously.

steps.title: Acclimatize mice and prepare for stimulation
steps.instruction: After arrival, allow mice to acclimatize for 1 h. Remove all enrichment items from the cage to prevent hiding. Ensure unlimited access to food and water. Schedule stimulation at the same time each day (e.g., 9–11 a.m.).

steps.title: Run 60‑Hz light stimulation protocol
steps.instruction: Start the appropriate Arduino program (60 Hz flicker or control). Expose the mice to light for 2 h per day for 5 consecutive days, keeping the box lid closed. This regimen yields ~40 % PNN reduction in V1. Note that the device generates electrical noise; additional shielding (e.g., copper mesh) is required for concurrent electrophysiology.

steps.title: Perfuse and collect tissue
steps.instruction: Four hours after the final 2‑hour stimulation session, perfuse the animals and harvest brain tissue for downstream PNN analysis (e.g., WFA staining, confocal imaging).
